We remark that DREM is only one example realization of the estimator class. For instance, recursive least-squares estimators with zonotopic uncertainty propagation also provide an adaptation law with a set-valued uncertainty certificate [13]. More generally, any adaptive, composite learning, or set-membership estimator can be used if it provides the adaptation law in (11) and an element-wise bound [11], [13].
We are now in a position to state the considered problem, which will be addressed using robust adaptive bCBFs.

Problem 1. Given the uncertain system (10), the safe set  $ \mathcal{C}_S $ in (2), and an element-wise certified adaptive estimator (11), design a control law  $ \boldsymbol{u} = \boldsymbol{k}(t, \boldsymbol{x}, \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \in \mathcal{U} $ that renders a subset of  $ \mathcal{C}_S $ forward invariant, ensuring the safety of (10).
### IV. MAIN RESULTS

We now develop the proposed robust adaptive bCBF method in four steps. First, we propagate the backup flow using the current parameter estimate. Second, we bound the mismatch between the true and estimated backup flows using the certified component-wise parameter error bounds. Third, we use this bound to define a tightened inner approximation of the implicit safe set. Fourth, we derive duality-based robust safety conditions that preserve a QP implementation.

Similar to the standard bCBF method outlined in Section II, the proposed approach leverages a backup controller  $ \boldsymbol{k}_{\mathrm{b}} : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{U} $ and a backup set  $ \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{B}} \subseteq \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{S}} $ given in (5). This time, we assume that  $ \boldsymbol{k}_{\mathrm{b}} $ is a robust backup controller.
Assumption 2. The backup controller  $ k_b $ renders  $ C_B $ forward invariant for (10) for any  $ \theta \in \Theta $.

In practice, robust backup sets can often be obtained by robustifying Lyapunov level sets around a stabilizable equilibrium point and verifying their invariance under the corresponding stabilizing feedback control law [9]. In Section V, we utilize this approach to synthesize a robust backup controller and a robust backup set for a quadrotor model.
We introduce the closed-loop dynamics of the system (10) under the robust backup controller as
$$ \dot{x}=f_{\mathrm{b}}(x,\theta)\triangleq f(x)+g(x)k_{\mathrm{b}}(x)+\psi_{\mathrm{b}}(x)\theta, $$
where  $ \psi_{b} $ indicates the regression matrix in (9) evaluated along the backup controller:
$$ \psi_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})\triangleq\phi(\boldsymbol{x},k_{\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})). $$
Then, the backup flow satisfies

$$ \begin{array}{r}{\frac{\partial}{\partial\tau}\varphi_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x})=f_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\varphi_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x}),\boldsymbol{\theta}\big),\quad\varphi_{\mathrm{b}}(0,\boldsymbol{x})=\boldsymbol{x}.}\end{array} $$

Ideally, one would use the backup flow to enforce the forward invariance of the implicit safe set  $ \mathcal{C}_I $ defined in (6). However, since the parameter  $ \theta $ is unknown, the backup flow  $ \varphi_b $ and the implicit set  $ \mathcal{C}_I $ may not be known. Therefore, we instead establish a known subset of  $ \mathcal{C}_I $ and enforce the forward invariance thereof. To this end, we propagate an estimated backup flow  $ \hat{\varphi}_b $ using the current parameter estimate  $ \hat{\theta}(t) $ that is frozen over the backup horizon:

$$ \begin{array}{r}{\frac{\partial}{\partial\tau}\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)=\boldsymbol{f}_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t),\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(t)\big),\quad\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(0,\boldsymbol{x},t)=\boldsymbol{x}.}\end{array} $$

While the estimated flow  $ \widehat{\varphi}_{b} $ is known, it is not sufficient for ensuring safety by itself, since the true parameter  $ \theta $ can differ from the estimated parameter  $ \hat{\theta} $. Therefore, we bound the difference between the true and estimated backup flows:
$$ \left\|\varphi_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x})-\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)\right\|\leq\delta_{\varphi}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t), $$
and use these bounds to establish robust safety. The following lemma provides one possible flow error bound  $ \delta_{\varphi} $.

Lemma 2. Assume that  $ f_b(x, \theta) $ in (17) is uniformly Lipschitz on  $ \mathcal{X} $ over all  $ \theta \in \Theta $ with Lipschitz constant  $ L_b $. Then, (21) holds for all  $ \tau \in [0, T] $,  $ \boldsymbol{x} \in \mathcal{X} $, and  $ t \geq 0 $ with

$$ \begin{align*}\delta_{\varphi}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)&\triangleq\int_{0}^{\tau}\mathrm{e}^{L_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau-s)}d_{\mathrm{b}}(s,\boldsymbol{x},t)ds,\\d_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)&\triangleq\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\|\boldsymbol{\psi}_{\mathrm{b},i}\big(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\varphi}}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)\big)\right\|_{\mathrm{s}}\rho_{i}(t),\end{align*} $$

where  $ \psi_{\mathrm{b},i} $ is the ith column of  $ \psi_{\mathrm{b}} $ in (18),  $ \|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{s}} $ represent a smooth upper bound of the Euclidean norm*, and  $ \rho_{i}(t) $ is the element-wise parameter estimation error bound in (13)

Proof. First, we derive the dynamics of the error term  $ e(\tau, \mathbf{x}, t) \triangleq \varphi_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau, \mathbf{x}) - \widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau, \mathbf{x}, t) $. Using (19) and (20), and adding and subtracting  $ f_{\mathrm{b}}(\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau, \mathbf{x}, t), \theta) $, we have

$$ \begin{align*}\frac{\partial}{\partial\tau}e(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)&=\boldsymbol{f}_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\varphi_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x}),\boldsymbol{\theta}\big)-\boldsymbol{f}_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t),\boldsymbol{\theta}\big)\\&\quad+\psi_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)\big)\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(t).\end{align*} $$
The last term can be bounded using  $ d_{b} $ as

$$ \begin{align*}\Big\|\psi_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)\big)\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(t)\Big\|&=\Bigg\|\sum_{i=1}^{N}\psi_{\mathrm{b},i}\big(\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)\big)\tilde{\theta}_{i}(t)\Bigg\|\\&\leq\sum_{i=1}^{N}\big\|\psi_{\mathrm{b},i}\big(\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)\big)\big\|_{\mathrm{s}}\rho_{i}(t)=d_{\mathrm{b}}(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t).\end{align*} $$
Next, using the integral form of the error dynamics and  $ e(0,x,t)=0 $, we get

$$ \begin{align*}\|e(\tau,\boldsymbol{x},t)\|\leq&\int_{0}^{\tau}\Big\|\boldsymbol{f}_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\varphi_{\mathrm{b}}(s,\boldsymbol{x}),\boldsymbol{\theta}\big)-\boldsymbol{f}_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(s,\boldsymbol{x},t),\boldsymbol{\theta}\big)\Big\|ds\\&+\int_{0}^{\tau}\Big\|\psi_{\mathrm{b}}\big(\widehat{\varphi}_{\mathrm{b}}(s,\boldsymbol{x},t)\big)\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(t)\Big\|ds,\\\leq&\int_{0}^{\tau}\big(L_{\mathrm{b}}\left\|\boldsymbol{e}(s,\boldsymbol{x},t)\right\|+d_{\mathrm{b}}(s,\boldsymbol{x},t)\big)ds,\end{align*} $$

where the first inequality follows from the triangle inequality

*In this work, we use  $ \|z\|_s = \sqrt{\|z\|^2 + \sigma^2} $ with  $ \sigma > 0 $, which is continuously differentiable and satisfies  $ \|z\|_s \geq \|z\| $ for all  $ z \in \mathbb{R}^n $.
